title: Connect two workstation ports and route the slack without disconnecting them
instruction: Plug the two blue cable ends into the green-marked ports on the two devices. Place the gold collar in the open cable guide and let go of both ends and the collar.
context: A shared workstation is ready to use when the two devices are connected and the slack is out of the working area. Routing a taut cable can pull an already inserted plug loose.
setup: On a 600 × 720 × 40 mm wood worktop, two 83 × 105 × 44 mm polymer device bases carry metal USB-C-style sockets. A blue-handled connector rests on each 53 × 42 × 49 mm support at reset. Their flexible jointed cable has a 16 × 16 × 11 mm gold collar with a raised grip and starts in a loose S-shape. The open guide has a 55 × 135 mm base and 16 mm side lips. Two YAM arms are mounted at worktop height. The README gives exact starting positions and material details.
scoring: Award 0.35 per correctly seated plug released for one second and still seated through routing and the trial end, with no gripper contact in the final second. In the real fixture, use video of the grip front in the 1.50 mm witness band at the marked port. With both plugs credited, award 0.30 if the released collar rests inside the outline for the final second. The README gives equivalent numeric simulation checks and instructions for observing the physical trial.
reset_notes: Return the two connectors to their stands and lay the cord in the authored S-shape with the collar outside the guide. Use scene seed 0.
fidelity: The passive physical fixture can be fabricated from the included dimensioned connector and guide geometry. Shell, socket, tongue, supports and guide interact through collision. Cable tension is approximated with jointed rigid segments. The task checks mechanical retention; neither simulated nor fabricated trainer uses electrical contacts.
